note: Cities on the globe. status: live (built and in web/data/<id>) or planned. Planned entries list the open data to check first; none of them has been verified for this project yet.
parked_note: Parked: built cities taken off the globe and out of the checks for now, to keep each round of checks short while work focuses on the others. Their data stays in cities/<id> and web/data/<id>. To bring one back, take its id off this list, rebuild the globe's list (python pipeline/pack.py) and run tools/check.sh <id>.

cities.name: Sydney
cities.summary: Central Sydney: 7,962 buildings, the Opera House and Harbour Bridge, sun access on protected public places, and a game: walk it, ride the ferries, fly under the bridge.

cities.name: Melbourne
cities.tagline: Docklands, the Hoddle Grid and Southbank to the Shrine
cities.summary: Central Melbourne from Docklands to the Shrine: 13,050 buildings on Geoscience Australia's 5 m LiDAR terrain, the Arts Centre spire, and sun on the public spaces the planning scheme protects.

cities.name: Melbourne Bayside
cities.tagline: St Kilda, Elwood and Brighton on Port Phillip
cities.summary: Port Phillip's shore from St Kilda to Brighton: 9,335 buildings, the 96 Brighton bathing boxes, Luna Park's Scenic Railway, and a game where little penguins come ashore on the St Kilda breakwater after sunset.

cities.name: Osaka
cities.summary: Umeda to Shinsekai along Midosuji, with Osaka Castle: 73,000 buildings, 89% of the roof area with a height measured for Project PLATEAU, the Dotonbori neon, a winter-sun study of the parks, and a game with Osaka people.

cities.name: Kyoto
cities.tagline: Kyoto Station and Kyoto Tower to the Imperial Palace
cities.summary: Central Kyoto, Kyoto Station to the Imperial Palace: 66,000 buildings with measured heights from Project PLATEAU, GSI laser terrain, and a game: walk the city with Kyoto people.

cities.name: Higashiyama
cities.tagline: Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, Ninenzaka and the Yasaka Pagoda
cities.summary: Kyoto's Higashiyama: Kiyomizu-dera's stage on its keyaki lattice, the stone lanes of Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka with their noren and lanterns, and the Yasaka Pagoda, on PLATEAU's measured heights.

cities.name: Fushimi Inari
cities.tagline: The Romon, the Senbon Torii and Mount Inari
cities.summary: Fushimi Inari Taisha: the Romon and the halls, the two tunnels of the Senbon Torii and thousands more torii climbing Mount Inari to Yotsutsuji and the summit, on PLATEAU's measured heights.

cities.name: Marunouchi & Ginza
cities.summary: Marunouchi to Tokyo Tower: 15,000 buildings, 76% of the footprint area at a PLATEAU-surveyed height, Tokyo Tower built to its published dimensions, and a game: Tokyo Station, the Palace, Hibiya Park, the water bus and a helicopter to the tower.
cities.tagline: Tokyo Station, the Palace, Ginza, the water bus and Tokyo Tower

cities.name: Shibuya
cities.summary: Sangenjaya to Shibuya, Harajuku and Yoyogi Park: 48,000 buildings at PLATEAU-surveyed heights, the scramble and Hachiko, SHIBUYA SKY's roof with its lift and escalator, Center Gai, Yoyogi's gymnasiums and the streets Persona 5 drew, from Sangenjaya's backstreets to the station.
cities.tagline: The scramble, Hachiko, SHIBUYA SKY, Center Gai and Sangenjaya's lanes

cities.name: Shinjuku
cities.summary: Nishi-Shinjuku's towers to Yotsuya: 27,000 buildings at PLATEAU-surveyed heights, Kabukicho's arch, the east exit's screens, 2-chome and Golden Gai, Shinjuku Gyoen, Jingu Gaien's ginkgo avenue and the Suga Shrine stairs of Your Name with this year's ema.
cities.tagline: Kabukicho, the east exit, Nishi-Shinjuku's towers and the Your Name stairs

cities.name: Asakusa
cities.tagline: Senso-ji, the Kaminarimon lantern, Nakamise and Tokyo Skytree across the Sumida
cities.summary: Asakusa and the Sumida from open data at PLATEAU-surveyed heights: Senso-ji's gates, pagoda and hall built to their published sizes, the Kaminarimon's lantern, Nakamise, the water bus, and Tokyo Skytree, 634 m, with a lift to the Tembo Deck.

cities.name: Akihabara
cities.tagline: Electric Town's signs on Chuo-dori, Kanda Myojin and Nikolai-do
cities.summary: Akihabara's Electric Town from open data at PLATEAU-surveyed heights: Chuo-dori's blade signs and wall prints, lit after dark, the arcades' lanes, Kanda Myojin's gate up the hill and Nikolai-do's dome over Ochanomizu.

cities.name: Ueno
cities.tagline: Ueno Park, Toshogu's gilt hall, Shinobazu Pond and Bentendo, and Ameyoko's market
cities.summary: Ueno from open data at PLATEAU-surveyed heights: the park on its hill with Saigo's statue, Toshogu's gilt hall between its lanterns and Kan'ei-ji's pagoda, Shinobazu Pond's lotus and Bentendo on its island, and Ameyoko's market under the tracks to Okachimachi.

cities.name: Ikebukuro
cities.tagline: Sunshine 60, Otome Road, the department stores and West Gate Park's ring
cities.summary: Ikebukuro from open data at PLATEAU-surveyed heights: Sunshine 60 over the east side, Sunshine 60-dori's signs and Otome Road's shops, the department stores' names round the station, and GLOBAL RING over West Gate Park.

cities.name: Jinbocho
cities.tagline: The book town's shops and carts, the Catholic Kanda Church and Nikolai-do
cities.summary: Jinbocho and Kanda from open data at PLATEAU-surveyed heights: the book town's second-hand shops along Yasukuni-dori with their carts of cheap books, the Catholic Kanda Church of 1928, and Nikolai-do over Ochanomizu.

cities.name: Roppongi
cities.tagline: Roppongi Hills and Maman, Keyakizaka's lights, the National Art Center and the crossing's bars
cities.summary: Roppongi from open data at PLATEAU-surveyed heights: Mori Tower and Maman the spider at Roppongi Hills, the Mohri Garden's pond, Keyakizaka's winter lights, the National Art Center's glass wave, Tokyo Midtown, and the bars round the crossing.

cities.name: Shinagawa
cities.tagline: Takanawa Gateway's folded roof, the station's two sides and the old Tokaido's post town
cities.summary: Shinagawa and Takanawa from open data at PLATEAU-surveyed heights: the station between the Takanawa hills and Konan's towers, Takanawa Gateway Station's folded roof, and the old Tokaido's first post town at Kita-Shinagawa with its shops and lanterns.

cities.name: Tsukishima
cities.tagline: Monja Street, Tsukuda's fishing village and Kachidoki Bridge
cities.summary: Tsukishima and Tsukuda from open data at PLATEAU-surveyed heights: Monja Street's seventy shops, Tsukuda's moat, its vermilion bridge and Sumiyoshi Shrine by the Sumida, the river's bridges, and Kachidoki Bridge's arches.

cities.name: Odaiba
cities.tagline: The Rainbow Bridge, the seaside park and its Statue of Liberty, and Fuji TV's sphere
cities.summary: Odaiba from open data at PLATEAU-surveyed heights: the Rainbow Bridge's towers and cables over the bay, the seaside park's beach and Statue of Liberty, Fuji TV's titanium sphere, and the Yurikamome's guideway across the islands.

cities.name: Whitsundays
cities.summary: The Whitsunday Islands and the inner Great Barrier Reef: 30 m survey bathymetry, a Sentinel-2 sea floor, caustics, wet sand and a swash line. Walk Whitehaven Beach, snorkel, dive.
cities.tagline: Whitehaven Beach, Hill Inlet and the Whitsunday Passage

cities.name: Hardy Reef
cities.tagline: Heart Reef and the Reefworld pontoon, outer reef
cities.summary: Hardy Reef on the outer Great Barrier Reef: Heart Reef, the Reefworld pontoon on the channel wall, and Hook, Line and Bait reefs, from 30 m survey bathymetry and Sentinel-2. No land: start on the pontoon's deck and dive the wall.

cities.name: Green Island
cities.tagline: Coral cay off Cairns, with Arlington Reef and Michaelmas Cay
cities.summary: Green Island, a coral cay 27 km off Cairns, with Arlington Reef, Upolu Cay and Michaelmas Cay: survey bathymetry, a seam-free Sentinel-2 sea floor and MSQ's tide. Walk the beach by the jetty, snorkel the reef flat.

cities.name: Heron Island
cities.tagline: Coral cay on the Tropic of Capricorn, with Wistari Reef
cities.summary: Heron Island and Heron and Wistari reefs in the southern Great Barrier Reef: the cay rebuilt from its mapped outline, the reef flat drying at low tide, the research station and the wreck of HMCS Protector at the channel.

cities.name: Lady Elliot Island
cities.tagline: The southernmost coral cay of the reef
cities.summary: Lady Elliot Island, the southernmost coral cay of the Great Barrier Reef: its platform reef in open water, the airstrip and old lighthouse, from survey bathymetry and Sentinel-2. Start on the western beach.

cities.name: New York
cities.data: NYC Open Data footprints with LiDAR roof heights; USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM; NYS orthoimagery.

cities.name: London
cities.data: Environment Agency 1 m LiDAR DTM (OGL); OSM heights; open aerial imagery still to find.

cities.name: Paris
cities.summary: Central Paris from the Eiffel Tower to the Île Saint-Louis: every roof measured by IGN's airborne LiDAR, zinc mansards with their dormers and chimney stacks, the Seine's bridges, and a game: ride the Batobus and fly under the Eiffel Tower.

cities.name: Amsterdam
cities.summary: Central Amsterdam from the IJ to Museumplein: every building the 3DBAG's model of it, measured by the national LiDAR, canal houses with the gable of their century, the church towers, and a game: read the gables, cross the IJ on the free ferry, find the winter sun.

cities.name: Hong Kong
cities.summary: Victoria Harbour from Central to Tsim Sha Tsui and the Peak: 7,513 buildings, nearly all at the heights the Lands Department surveyed, checked against a 2020 LiDAR scan; the Bank of China Tower, HSBC and the Star Ferry; and a game: ride the ferry and the Peak Tram.

cities.name: Singapore
cities.data: OSM footprints and heights; open bare-earth DEM and imagery still to find.

Melbourne.summary: Two districts of Melbourne on Geoscience Australia's LiDAR terrain: the city centre from Docklands to the Shrine, and Port Phillip's shore from St Kilda to Brighton, where little penguins come ashore after sunset.

Tokyo.summary: Tokyo as maps, the way games draw it: each district a walkable map of its own, chosen from the subway map. Lit stations are built; grey ones are next.
Tokyo.note: Districts and lines from the Tokyo Metro and JR East maps; station positions are the stations' own (OpenStreetMap). Which districts a game sends you to follows Persona 5's Tokyo (Atlus, 2016): Shibuya, Shinjuku, Akihabara, Asakusa, Ueno, Ikebukuro, Odaiba, Jinbocho, Kanda, Tsukishima.
